- When sentiment is consistently bullish (positive) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 5–10% for 30-day horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward bias of 3–5% in next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment turns bearish (negative) mid-period, model frequently underreacts — adjust forecast downward by 2–4% per negative sentiment day.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 2–5% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model often overfits short-term noise — use 10-day moving average as baseline for smoothing forecast deviations.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 50% of 30-day forecast range, model is overconfident — apply 5–10% downward correction.
